memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "If you do not carefully follow all the words of this law, which are written in this book, and do not revere this glorious and awesome name — the Lord your God — the Lord will send fearful plagues on you and your descendants, harsh and prolonged disasters, and severe and lingering illnesses." — Deut 28:58-59 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Notice what God places at the very centre of faithfulness here: to "revere this glorious and awesome name — the Lord your God." Underneath all the commands and warnings lies this one heart posture — reverence for who God is. The root of obedience is awe. When people lose their reverence for God, disobedience of every kind follows.

We live in an age that has largely lost this sense of awe before God. He is often spoken of casually, as a comfortable friend or a distant idea, but rarely as the "glorious and awesome" One before whom heaven bows. Yet a right relationship with God begins with reverence — a deep, humble wonder at His greatness and holiness.

This reverence is not cold fear that drives us away from God. It is the awe that draws us to worship. The Bible calls the fear of the Lord the beginning of wisdom (Prov 9:10). To revere God's name is to take Him seriously, to treasure Him, to live in the light of His majesty.

And wonderfully, this glorious and awesome God has made His name known to us most fully in Jesus. The name of Jesus is the name above every name, at which one day every knee will bow (Phil 2:10). To revere God's name is to honour Christ, in whom the fullness of God's glory shines. Let awe rekindle your worship, and let reverence be the root of a life that gladly follows Him.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Have I lost some of my reverence and awe before God?
2. Do I treat God's name and presence as holy?
3. How can I cultivate deeper wonder at God's greatness this week?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Glorious and awesome God, forgive me when I have grown casual toward You. Restore my reverence and wonder, and help me honour Your holy name in all I do. Amen.
